Cc: Chris Morton <chris.morton@peridot.io>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro + pilot exploration

Hi Rachel —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap from our side and what we want to validate in a short pilot: 

- Goal: Evaluate whether Redwood can reduce per-request latency on our customer-facing summarization endpoint and keep token costs predictable.
- Scope we propose: 3-week staged pilot against a subset (3 customer flows, ~50k tokens/day peak).
- Must-haves: privacy controls (no data retention beyond session), predictable latency under 200ms p50, and a simple failover path if throughput is exceeded.

Next asks from Peridot:
1) A short pilot charter we can agree on (owners, timeline, success metrics).
2) Security snapshot for our InfoSec review (SOC2, retention controls).
3) High-level runbook for test data ingestion and traffic shaping.

Can your team share a charter template and a proposed owner map? We can have our infra lead (Chris) make time for a tech sync this week if that helps.

Thanks —
Alyssa
Alyssa Chen
Head of Product, Peridot Systems

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@peridot.io>, Chris Morton <chris.morton@peridot.io>

Subject: Staged pilot charter & owner rotation — next steps

Thanks Alyssa — great to meet you both. Recapping and proposing a concrete next step so we can move straight into a controlled pilot window.

Summary (agrees with your points):
- Objective: Confirm latency and cost profile for the 3 customer flows while validating data controls.
- Proposed duration: 3 weeks (staged):
  - Week 0 (prep): data access, infra checks, security signoff
  - Week 1 (ingest + smoke tests): run synthetic traffic and KV cache warm-up
  - Week 2 (load + regression): real-ish traffic shape, monitor quality regressions
  - Week 3 (evaluation & handoff): collect metrics, readout and decision

Success criteria (proposed):
- Latency: p50 < 200ms, p95 < 600ms for target flows under baseline traffic
- Cost: per-inference token cost within 20% of estimated baseline (we'll provide cost modeling)
- Data controls: no retention beyond session; keys stored in your KMS; access logs available

Owner map (redwood / peridot):
- Pilot owner (commercial): Rachel Kim / Alyssa Chen
- Technical lead (redwood): Ben Carter (cc'd) — infra & runtime tuning
- Technical lead (peridot): Chris Morton — dataset access & network config
- Security / compliance: Lauren Bishop (redwood) to share security snapshot; Peridot InfoSec to confirm

Attachments I am including: pilot-charter-template.xlsx (editable starter), security-snapshot-2026.pdf (high-level)
Links: pilot folder (Drive) + HubSpot deal (attached in metadata)

Immediate asks to unblock (can we get these by end of week?):
1) Peridot confirms pilot owner & approves the charter (reply OK to the attached sheet).
2) Chris to share sample traffic schema / S3 access details or an alternative for data ingestion.
3) Peridot InfoSec: confirm which controls need the deeper evidence (we'll queue that).

If you want a 20-minute tech sync later today I can have Ben join. Otherwise, if the owner map looks good, we can lock Week 0 activities and send calendar invites.

Best,
Rachel Kim

Thanks — quick technical follow-ups so we scope Week 0 correctly: 

1) Sample data: for the smoke tests we only need a masked subset of customer payloads (JSON schema + ~500 examples). If you can drop to an S3 bucket with a short-lived key that speeds things up.
2) Network: does Peridot prefer a private peering (VPC) or public egress with allowlist? For a short pilot public egress + IP allowlist works fine but we can do VPC if you need encryption in flight within your VPC.
3) Tokens & rate shape: can you share a 24-hr sample traffic shape (peak qps, avg token length)? We'll prepare batching and cache parameters to meet p50 targets.

Proposed quick schedule: 30-min infra sync tomorrow at 9:30am PT — I'll send invite if that slot works.
